title: The same wall, one level up
caption: Same new colleague, same wall. The value arrives when you reinvest.

complementary-investment.description: General-purpose technologies "enable and require significant complementary investments" in processes and human capital, often intangible, so gains show up late.[1]

adoption-without-impact.description: In a survey of about 6,000 executives, about 69% of firms use AI while roughly 90% report no effect on productivity or employment over three years.[1]

disputed-headline.description: The "95% of pilots fail" figure is the MIT NANDA report's own directional, interview-based number, read here from a third-party copy; a Wharton survey of about 800 leaders found nearly three in four see positive ROI, also self-reported. Neither settles the true share, so do not lead with 95%.[1][2]

not-only-you.title: Not only you
not-only-you.script: And it is not only you. A team hits the same wall. So does a whole company. Everyone gets the same new colleague, and nobody hands them a day-one note.

adopted-not-absorbed.title: Adopted, not absorbed
adopted-not-absorbed.script: One large survey of about six thousand executives found that most firms use AI, yet most see no effect on their output so far. Leaders asked about it themselves sound more upbeat. Nobody knows the true share. The tools came in, and the way of working stayed exactly as it was.

reinvest.title: Reinvest
reinvest.keywords: new skills, new disciplines, across the organization
reinvest.script: So the value does not arrive by itself. It arrives when you reinvest. The effort AI saves you goes back in, as new skills and new disciplines. For you. For your team. Across the whole organization. AI does not remove the work. It moves it.
